title: UCP discovery and capability negotiation (two layers)
summary: Negotiation happens in two layers. First the platform picks one protocol version profile from the business profile. Then, on each request, the business intersects capabilities by exact version and prunes extensions whose parent is not in the result. The example shows a cart capability dropped because only the platform lists it, and a loyalty extension dropped because only the business lists it.

steps.label: GET /.well-known/ucp
steps.detail: Discovery is optional (MAY) but common. The business profile is public by design.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, spec version 2026-08-25.
GET /.well-known/ucp HTTP/1.1
Host: shop.example

steps.label: Profile: version, supported_versions, capabilities
steps.detail: The business lists ucp.version 2026-08-25 and, in supported_versions, a leaf profile for 2026-04-08. Its capabilities are checkout, fulfillment (extends checkout) and loyalty (extends checkout).

steps.label: Layer 1: select version 2026-08-25
steps.detail: The platform should prefer the newest version it supports. If it chose 2026-04-08 it would fetch that leaf profile and check that its ucp.version equals 2026-04-08. Leaf profiles must not contain supported_versions.

failures.outcome: version_unsupported (REST 422) as a transport error, with an optional continue_url.

steps.label: Request with UCP-Agent: profile="..."
steps.detail: The platform names its own profile on every request. Over MCP the same URL travels in meta["ucp-agent"].profile inside the tool arguments.

steps.label: GET platform profile
steps.detail: The business fetches and validates the platform profile unless it has a cached copy. The platform lists checkout, fulfillment and cart.

failures.condition: Not valid JSON or violates the schema

steps.label: Layer 2: intersect and prune
steps.detail: Kept: checkout and fulfillment, which both list at 2026-08-25. Dropped: cart (only the platform lists it) and loyalty (only the business lists it). Pruning then removes any extension whose parents are all gone and repeats until stable; fulfillment survives because checkout is present.

steps.label: Response ucp envelope: version and active capabilities
steps.detail: The business includes the version used, the active capabilities and the payment handlers for this checkout in every response, so the platform always knows which schema applies. The handlers are omitted in this abbreviated example.
